S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a marked, persistent fear of a clearly defined object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger and leads to avoidance or significant distress. The feared stimulus almost invariably elicits an immediate anxiety response, and the person either avoids it or endures it with intense discomfort, often recognizing that the fear is excessive or unreasonable. The condition tends to have a chronic course if untreated but may fluctuate in intensity depending on life circumstances and exposure demands. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by its narrow, circumscribed focus (e.g., particular animals, heights, injections, flying) and by the absence of broader worries, obsessions, or panic attacks occurring in a wide range of situations.

patient.personality: Jerrel is a meticulous, intellectually curious planner who channels his vivid imagination into technology consulting and abstract art, but tends to ruminate and worry late into the night.
patient.stressor: Around a year and a couple of months ago, Jerrel accompanied his wife to a routine outpatient procedure at a hospital, where he unexpectedly witnessed a medical emergency in the adjacent bay involving another patient who rapidly decompensated during an injection. The sudden flurry of alarms, staff shouting, and the sight of needles and IV lines being hurriedly managed imprinted itself on him, dovetailing with his lifelong tendency to visualize worst‑case scenarios in vivid detail. In the months after that incident, he found himself going to considerable lengths to avoid routine blood work and vaccinations recommended by his primary care doctor, rescheduling or canceling appointments and delegating any in‑person tech support at medical clients’ offices to younger colleagues. Over the past year, his avoidance has started to interfere with managing his own chronic health conditions and created conflict with his wife, who worries about his skipped appointments, which finally persuaded him to seek psychiatric evaluation when he realized he was risking his health to stay away from a very specific medical procedure setting.
patient.chief_complaint: “Every time I even think about getting stuck with a needle now, my body reacts instantly like I’m back in that treatment room and I just can’t go through with it.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that day in the hospital, the idea of anyone coming at me with a syringe or IV line feels wildly dangerous, like my brain insists that a routine flu shot is on the verge of turning into some catastrophic code blue, even though I know rationally that’s not how it works.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I so much as open the patient portal and see a reminder for lab work, my heart starts pounding, my chest tightens, and I’m suddenly back in that bay hearing the alarms and shouting, like my body has hit a panic button before I’ve even finished reading the message.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’ll cancel or push back appointments, route my consulting calls to Zoom instead of going into clinics, and if I absolutely can’t avoid a necessary blood draw I sit there gripping the chair, breathing shallowly, staring at the wall and white‑knuckling my way through it while every part of me is screaming to get up and walk out.
